source_review.notes: Checked W3C DCAT 3, DQV, PROV-O, SKOS, DCMI Metadata Terms, W3C SHACL, the OpenLineage object model, Apache Atlas 2.0.0, the current OpenMetadata architecture documentation, and the DataHub architecture overview. All ten primary or official destinations returned HTTP 200 after replacing an obsolete versioned OpenMetadata path with its supported latest URL. Claims remain bounded to catalog vocabularies, provenance, quality, graph validation, lineage event structure, and documented product architectures; design recommendations are identified as architectural synthesis.

evidence: Reviewed the catalog capability tuple K and its identity, entity, assertion, graph, vocabulary, provenance, ingestion, discovery, workflow, security, operation, and lifecycle components.

Checked notation for cataloged resources and records, distributions and services, qualified assertions, resolved precedence, temporal graphs, source snapshots, missing candidates, projection offsets, authorized candidates, ranking, eligibility, field coverage, quality measurements, freshness, identity resolution, and fitness.
Verified that source observation time, resource lifecycle, catalog acceptance, projection time, and data freshness are not collapsed into one timestamp.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation supports scoped catalog reasoning without claiming that a record, search rank, graph path, or metadata badge establishes truth or fitness.

evidence: Executed catalog-reconciliation-and-search-eligibility with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced the declared eleven-line output.
Confirmed six records include five active, six documented, five owned, one stale, and one orphaned asset.
Confirmed four asserted edges include one dangling target, while three lexical candidates become two eligible results and orders ranks first.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The recomputation covers invented records, one substring query, one freshness threshold, and one deterministic score; it does not evaluate a production catalog.

evidence: Verified a metadata assertion includes resource, predicate, value, source, agent, observation time, effective interval, confidence, method, and lifecycle state.
Checked missing-candidate set difference against an explicitly complete source snapshot and confirmed it is not equated directly with deletion.
Verified search candidate authorization precedes ranking and that metadata coverage, quality measurement, freshness, identity resolution, and fitness each name their own scope.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The symbolic review separates resource from record, accepted store from projection, observation from authority, relevance from eligibility, and discovery from access.

evidence: Reviewed source authority, environment, resource type, catalog record, distribution, service, field, assertion, relation, vocabulary, domain, tenant, viewer, consumer, and retention boundaries.

Tested rename, recreation, merge, split, permission loss, partial crawl, old snapshot, duplicate event, late event, dangling edge, false Cartesian lineage, projection drift, high-degree graph, stale quality, and missing owner cases.

Reviewed autocomplete and facet leakage, sensitive schemas and query logs, embedding deletion, connector privilege and injection, popularity feedback, cross-domain partial results, tombstone replay, backup restore, and migration loss.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary cases prevent a successful crawl, nonempty field, reachable node, high rank, green check, current index, or restored database from standing in for governed correctness.

evidence: Traced distinct resource and record identity, assertion provenance, field-level precedence, rebuildable projections, cautious absence, secure retrieval, separate fitness signals, qualified lineage, federation authority, replayable change, access separation, and full closure throughout the chapter.
Verified ingestion, conflict resolution, search, graph traversal, workflows, active metadata, replication, recovery, and migration retain stable identity and temporal evidence.

Checked all decision, scope, identity, model, authority, ingestion, absence, graph, vocabulary, quality, projection, discovery, workflow, automation, protection, operations, recovery, and closure gates.
invariant_checking.notes: The invariants keep catalog state attributable, time-aware, identity-safe, projection-reconcilable, authorization-aware, operationally recoverable, and historically interpretable.

evidence: Reviewed the eighteen assurance gates as a trace from user decisions and scope through identity, assertions, ingestion, projections, discovery, governance, operation, recovery, and retirement.

Checked counterexamples to catalog-is-inventory, page-is-resource, name-is-identity, missing-is-deleted, graph-path-is-lineage, rank-is-fitness, tag-is-policy, federation-is-many-connectors, and reindex-is-repair claims.
Verified catalog fitness is conditional on meaning, authority, quality, freshness, policy, access, support, consumer context, and time rather than inferred from presence.
proof_review.notes: The chapter provides an architectural assurance framework and counterexamples, not a formal proof that a catalog is complete, truthful, secure, relevant, or beneficial.

evidence: Audited uses of authoritative, canonical, complete, observed, declared, inferred, reviewed, current, fresh, valid, conforming, related, derived, relevant, eligible, trusted, certified, active, deprecated, retired, and deleted.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from discovery purpose and source standards through identity, assertions, ingestion, temporal reconciliation, graphs, vocabularies, quality, search, workflows, active metadata, federation, security, operation, migration, and closure.
